key_insight: A Fourier neural operator learns a fast correction from inexpensive Boussinesq simulations to expensive compressible-flow reference solutions, greatly improving natural-convection accuracy with one model evaluation per case.
engineering_relevance: This enables more accurate CFD predictions for heat-driven flows while preserving much of the computational efficiency of low-fidelity incompressible solvers.
method: Generate matched simulation pairs from Boussinesq and compressible flow models.
Train a Fourier neural operator surrogate on these paired fields.
Use an implicit monolithic mixed FEM implementation in FEniCSx and validate against COMSOL and literature benchmarks.
evidence_signal: Across 2D and 3D tests, the surrogate achieved SSIM close to 1 for all flow variables and reduced mean-squared error by roughly one to nearly three orders of magnitude versus Boussinesq outputs.
watch_item: Performance depends on high-quality paired training data and careful dataset generation; extrapolation beyond the training distribution may be unreliable.
paper_title: A Neural Surrogate Approach for Simulating Natural Convection Problems
